text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Christian Maronite Patriarch Sfeir ended his visit to Rome and Brazil and returned to Lebanon. "Lebanon and Syria have some problems that need to be solved," he said.
-Italy's Prime Minister Prodi -- expected in Beirut on an official visit on Tuesday -- said in Rome: "Beirut is closer to us than Berlin".
-Net public debt reached $10.890 billion at the end of February 1997.
-Egypt's Foreign Minsiter Moussa attacked a Lebanese decision to ban imports of Egyptian potatoes and said countermeasures against Lebanon might be in order.
Lebanon's Agriculture Minister Fakhoury defended his decision by saying it was not aimed at Egypt but to protect home-grown potatoes.
-House Speaker Berri stressed the right of all Lebanese, in Lebanon and outside it to take part in the country's political life.

-Arab League Secretary-General Abdel-Meguid said during his visit to Lebanon that an Arab mini-summit may be held soon to discuss measures to counter Israel's plans to build a settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
